Super Micro (SMCI) has plunged 32% in a month, and a record revenue beat can't hide gross margins sinking to 13% from 18%.

Dell and Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) have fallen 35% and 29%, showing Super Micro's slide is part of a sector-wide AI hardware unwind.

Bulls see 82% upside and a 5x P/E; CFO Mark Long's warning of thinner second-half margins makes this a bargain or falling knife.

Released: The Definitive Guide to Retirement Income. It is a free guide from Fisher Investments covering what your retirement will really cost, where the cash flow should come from, and how much you can safely withdraw each year. Learn more here. Learn More Here › (sponsor)

The AI hardware trade is reversing, and the server makers that rode it higher are giving back ground fast. Super Micro Computer (NASDAQ:SMCI) stock is down 32% over the past month and recently traded at $22.56. The selling continues, with Super Micro stock down 8% from the prior session's close.

anandaBGD / Getty Images

Tech stocks are trimming some of the prior session's gains, with NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA) slipping. AI server and hardware names are reversing along with it, which places Super Micro's slide inside a sector-wide unwind. The open question is whether that selloff has made the company cheap enough to lure value hunters.

What Pulled Super Micro Lower Over the Past Month

Super Micro reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $19.9 billion on November 3, above its original guidance range of $14.5 billion to $15.5 billion. Within that total was $2.3 billion of deployments originally scheduled for earlier periods, and underlying revenue without the catch-up was approximately $17.6 billion. The company's generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) gross margin fell to 12.7%, down from the 17.5% it posted in Q4 FY2026.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 8% in the week ended November 20, its worst week since March 2020, while the S&P 500 fell 8.6% and the Nasdaq Composite dropped 10%, Yahoo Finance reported. Friday's sell-off pushed both the Dow and the S&P 500 into correction territory, and the Nasdaq Composite fell 5.28%, which wiped out its gain for 2026. Investors were increasingly concerned about technology valuations and the prospect of higher interest rates, and Reuters reported that the S&P 500 notched its seventh consecutive drop, its longest losing streak since February 2020.

A Rout Driven by Valuations

The slide had been building for days. Yahoo Finance reported that the Dow sank 850 points on November 17, with attention on a closely watched earnings report from a leading AI chipmaker. Duality Research noted that day that the S&P 500 technology sector's forward price-to-earnings ratio had fallen to 17.2 times, its lowest level since 2020. The firm added that the sector's gains for the year were almost entirely attributable to multiple expansion, which means investors had been paying more for the same earnings rather than earning more. Our ranking of the best cheap stocks heading into 2027 covers one way readers have looked for value after a drop like this.

Some See a Pause, Not a Break

Not everyone read the sell-off as a break in the market. Ed Yardeni, founder of Yardeni Research, maintained a cautiously bullish outlook and described the sell-off as a necessary rest for the market, Yahoo Finance reported. Markets rebounded sharply on Monday, November 23, when Yahoo Finance reported the Dow up more than 3% and the Nasdaq Composite up more than 6% after the AI chipmaker reinstated its former chief executive. The same report said UBS saw markets pricing a near-certain 25-basis-point Federal Reserve rate hike in December, so the interest rate concern had not gone away. Revenue growth is one measure that does not depend on the multiple investors are willing to pay for each dollar of earnings.

The stocks below all grew revenue by more than 15% in the latest quarter and over the past 12 months, trade under $50 per share, and have market capitalizations above $10 billion. Wall Street staged a strong rebound yesterday as investors returned to beaten-down technology and semiconductor stocks following NVIDIA's NVDA decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO. The S&P 500 rose 4.7%, the Nasdaq Composite jumped 6.5% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 3%, with NVIDIA shares soaring more than 31%. The sharp recovery has revived optimism around the AI and semiconductor sectors after a period of intense selling pressure.

However, rather than chasing stocks that have already rebounded sharply, investors may also want to look beyond the technology rally for fundamentally strong companies trading at attractive valuations. Several quality stocks have been weighed down by broader macroeconomic concerns and market volatility despite their earnings potential and long-term business prospects. This creates an opportunity to identify undervalued stocks with improving earnings outlooks before the broader market fully recognizes their potential.

In periods of heightened market volatility and economic uncertainty, value investing can offer an attractive alternative to growth- or momentum-driven strategies. When investors sell stocks amid broader market concerns, fundamentally sound companies can become available at discounted valuations, creating opportunities for value investors to capitalize on their long-term earnings potential.

However, identifying genuinely undervalued stocks requires more than simply looking for low share prices or valuation multiples. Several stocks that have delivered significant gains in the past demonstrate the potential of this investment strategy. Here, we discuss four stocks — Arrow Electronics ARW, Super Micro Computer SMCI, BP plc BP and Ingram Micro Holding Corporation INGM — that have qualified our PEG-driven screening criteria.

However, this apparently simple value investment technique has some drawbacks and not understanding the strategy properly may often lead to "value traps." In such a situation, these value picks start to underperform over the long run as the temporary problems, which once drove the share price down, turn out to be persistent.

There are many value investment yardsticks, such as dividend yield, P/E or P/B, which are simple and can single out whether a stock is trading at a discount.

However, for investors looking to escape such value traps, it is also vital to determine where the stock would be headed in the next 12 to 24 months. Warren Buffett advises these investors to focus on the earnings growth potential of a stock. This is where lies the importance of a not-so-popular value investing metric, the PEG ratio.

Today's big story: Nvidia Added $954 Billion In A Day. Is Jensen Huang Too Big To Fire?

Weak cash has rarely hurt Dell stock after its reports. Since early 2020, the cash Dell's business brought in, called operating cash flow, fell short of its profit in 6 of 27 reported quarters. The stock rose the next trading day in 5 of those 6. The median one-day gain was 7.4%.

Dell Technologies reports again today, Tuesday, Nov 24. Its latest quarter has the largest dollar gap between cash and profit of the six. In the three months to Jul 31, 2026, Dell made $4.1 billion of profit. It brought in only $2.2 billion of operating cash. That is 53.8 cents of cash for each dollar of profit.

Sales are not the worry. Dell's revenue in that quarter rose 57.7% from a year earlier. This article looks at cash instead, and at what the stock did after past quarters like this one.

Why did Dell stock jump on Monday?

Monday was a big day for AI hardware stocks. U.S. stocks rose after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO. The S&P 500 rose 4.7% that day. Nvidia's jump was the day's big story. These are the moves from Friday's close to Monday's close:

Nvidia rose 31.5%.

Dell rose 20.5% to $334.91.

Hewlett Packard Enterprise rose 17.4%.

Super Micro Computer rose 13.3%.

HP Inc. rose 3.4%.

We found no confirmed Dell-specific reason for its jump. On Friday the stock had closed at $278.02, 52.7% below its closing high of $588.40 on Sep 17.

Even after Monday's 20.5% jump, Dell closed 43.1% below its Sep 17 high. If you are holding cash back and waiting for a calmer price, that money can still earn something while it waits. Key Takeaways

Dell fell 27% in a month with Super Micro and Nvidia, even after Monday's rebound.

Estimates barely moved, so the selloff came out of the multiple, now back near its average.

Signed-deal price hikes and HPE's nearly doubled server sales point to stronger demand than Steve Eisman expects.

Dell's loans to its own customers are the main risk, so its Nov. 24 report needs to show cash catching up.

Dell Technologies (DELL:NYSE) is down 27% over the past month, more than three times the Nasdaq 100's drop, even after Monday's 20% jump. Rival Super Micro Computer (SMCI:NASDAQ) and chip supplier Nvidia (NVDA:NASDAQ) fell 26% and 22%, and almost none of the drop came from Dell's own numbers.

On a Nov. 13 episode of The Real Eisman Playbook, Steve Eisman said: "The picks and shovels companies like Arista, Cisco and Dell will also slow along with NVIDIA, proportionate to the slowdown in data center build out."

Since then, rival Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE:NYSE) has reported server revenue up 94.7% to $8.8 billion.

Three Blows, and None of Them Dell's

Intel's Oct. 29 PC warning came first. Then Texas elected a governor who promised a data center moratorium. Then came Nvidia's CEO crisis and a report tracing 22 Dell servers with banned Nvidia chips to Shanghai (Dell cut off that buyer in February 2025).

Dell's estimates barely moved. Analysts expect normalized EPS of $25.86 for the year ending January 2027 and $30.55 the year after, against $25.90 and $29.93 before the slide:

DELL Normalized EPS and Estimates: Fiscal 2024-2029 (TIKR)

So the selloff hit the multiple. Dell's forward P/E fell to 9.8x on Nov. 20, below its five-year average of 12x and far under August's 26x:

DELL Stock NTM P/E: 5-Year (TIKR)

Monday's jump put it back near that average.

Buyers Are Still Paying Up

The Financial Times reported on Nov. 22 that Dell, HPE, Lenovo and Super Micro want up to 45% more on AI server deals signed months ago, as memory costs soar. XTX is suing Dell over a $62 million to $70 million ask on a $549 million order, but some buyers, including Jane Street, are reportedly paying because capacity is scarce. A slowing build-out wouldn't look like this.

HPE's results Monday night fit that picture: its Cloud & AI operating margin rose to 18.4% from 9.3%.

Key Takeaways

Dell fell 11% on Friday, then jumped 20.5% on Monday, a day before its Nov. 24 report.

Jim Cramer says Dell can be ridden through the selloff, but a 21% gross margin leaves little room.

AI servers earn a mid-single-digit operating margin. Super Micro's and HP's margins have slipped; HPE's Cloud & AI segment just posted 18.4%.

Monday's rebound took Dell to about 12x forward earnings, near its five-year average.

Dell Technologies (DELL:NYSE) fell 11% on Friday, Nov. 20, in a broad tech selloff, then jumped 20.5% to $334.91 on Monday after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO. It reports its fiscal third quarter on Tuesday, Nov. 24, after the close.

Super Micro Computer (SMCI:NASDAQ) and Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE:NYSE) compete with Dell for the same AI server orders, and HP Inc. (HPQ:NYSE) buys the same memory chips for its PCs.

On Thursday's Mad Money, a caller down about 34% on Dell in the last three months asked Jim Cramer what he thought of the stock now:

"I think Dell is one of the few companies that can be ridden through here. You have to accept the fact that at 312 it could go down to 250, but you have to be willing to buy it at 250."

Dell closed Friday at $278.02, more than halfway from $312 to his $250. On Monday it closed at $334.91, back above the $312 he cited.

The pushback is about margin, not demand. Dell earned a 21.0% gross margin last quarter, thin for a company at the center of the AI buildout. Tuesday's report should show which side is right.

The orders are there

In its quarter to July 31, Dell booked $60.9 billion of AI server orders and ended with a $95 billion AI server backlog. For the quarter it reports Tuesday, it guided to $19 billion of AI server revenue.

Dell Fell 37% Before Its November 24 Report. Now Its Thin Margin Has to Hold ©Erik Mclean from Pexels, Grailify from Pexels via Canva
Key Takeaways

Dell Technologies stock fell 37% in the month to Nov. 20, then rebounded 20.5% on Nov. 23, a day before its fiscal third-quarter report.

Analysts still expect $25.86 of normalized EPS for the year ending January 2027, yet the stock trades at its five-year average of 11.8x forward earnings.

HPE just showed server makers can pass on memory costs. Dell has to show the same.

Dell Technologies (DELL:NYSE) stock fell 37% in the month to Nov. 20, then jumped 20.5% on Nov. 23 to close at $334.91. It reports fiscal third-quarter results after the close on Nov. 24.

On Nov. 22, the Financial Times reported that Dell, Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE:NYSE), Lenovo and Supermicro are demanding up to 45% more for AI servers months after customers signed contracts. HP Inc. (HPQ:NYSE), which reports the same evening as Dell, faces the same rising memory costs in its PCs.

Wall Street Hasn't Blinked

Analysts have barely touched their numbers. Consensus normalized EPS for Dell's fiscal 2027 is $25.86, about 2.5x the $10.30 it earned in fiscal 2026:

DELL Normalized EPS, Actual and Consensus Estimates: Fiscal 2025-2029 (TIKR)

That sits a bit above Dell's own non-GAAP guide of $25.50. With $11.90 earned in the first half and $6.50 guided for the third quarter, the guide needs $7.10 in the fourth quarter and the consensus $7.46, both above the $7.04 Dell earned in the second quarter.

The market isn't convinced. Even after the Nov. 23 rebound, Dell trades at 11.8x forward earnings, level with its five-year average and far from the 26x it reached on Aug. 13:

DELL Stock NTM P/E: 5-Year (TIKR)

TIKR Tracks 29 Analysts on Dell Technologies. How Many Say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Dell Technologies, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Dell Technologies' Analyst Ratings

21% Is the Line to Hold

Dell's gross margin was 21.0% in the quarter to July 31, back up from 17.9% the quarter before but below the 24.9% of the quarter to Feb. 2, 2024:

DELL Quarterly Gross Margin: 3-Year (TIKR)

That rebound came even as AI servers, which management says earn a mid-single-digit operating margin, grew to 51.6% of Infrastructure Solutions Group (ISG) revenue. Dell raised prices as component costs climbed, lifting product gross margin to 17.3% from 12.1% a year earlier.

Holding it will be harder this quarter. Dell guides $19 billion of AI server revenue, about 39% of its $49 billion revenue guide against about 35% last quarter, and an ISG operating margin just over 13.4%, down from 15.0%. Repricing signed orders protects the margin only if customers pay up.

President Trump went on CNBC Monday morning and said out loud what traders had long suspected. Asked whether last week's selloff factored into his push to put Jensen Huang back in charge of NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA), he answered: "Probably so, but the bigger impact was the long term." He told CNBC's Eamon Javers he spoke to the board and "convinced them," adding, "I made the deal." Trump said he dialed into Nvidia's board meeting by phone and called his intervention "very important" to Huang's return.

Drew Angerer / Getty Images

A sitting president just described a reflex in his own words. When stocks fall hard enough, the White House picks up the phone.

Wall Street Priced the Backstop in Minutes

Nvidia climbed 31.31% in Monday's regular session, from $125.53 to $164.83, on pace for its biggest intraday gain since 2003, according to Hedgeye. The SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY) rose 4.85%. Super Micro Computer (NASDAQ:SMCI), whose server business lives on Nvidia's chip roadmap, gained 14.11%.

NVDA Price Scenario — 24/7 Wall St.

At 11:00 a.m. ET, Bloomberg ETF analyst Eric Balchunas named the trade: "Trump Put in effect.." He grouped it with the Fed Put and the Vanguard Put as reasons he stays bullish long term.
